body: we still have a reasonable amount of people who go from InstantSearch v1 -> v4, can we keep this, but as a development warning?
does the middleware not have an unsubscribe possibility? (could be returned from the subscribe call, not sure if useful)

```suggestion
      this.middlewares.push(newMiddleware);
```

(also needs to be updated in more places if this is chosen
Ah no, I see it's separate, makes sense!
this makes sense, but I don't see it in the previous implementation, what am I missing?
We already removed this error in #4119. I was surprised it was still here. We might have messed up the history.

It used to be here:

https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch.js/blob/49ffca2d781d2125250bdcb111d2f1dc0c43e740/src/lib/InstantSearch.ts#L258-L262

It's now part of the middleware. Note that this is a side effect though, so not that great.
The `Routing` type defined in `InstantSearch.ts` could be merged with this interface, no?
Could work for now but like you said this is not great. Maybe we could introduce more handlers to address these cases later?

Would have gone with simply `router` instead of `createRouter` here. I found this more natural when using it with `this.use()`: `this.use(router(options))`

WDYT?

Yes, I'll think it through. What do you mean by "handlers"?

We could still replicate the logic in the original `InstantSearch.ts` but I was reluctant to it at first because I didn't want this entry to be dependant on the router. The technical solution would be to mutate those in the constructor by importing the basic `stateMapping` and reading it from here. But I wanted it completely detached so that we don't need to import this package if we don't use it. What I'm aiming here is to make the package more easily modular so people load only the parts of the code they need. Do you think this side effect is an OK tradeoff?
Sure! I didn't know if there were any naming convention for middleware.

Note that the word `router` will be repeated:

```js
router({ router, stateMapping })
```

Not too sure then. The name is internal for now so I think it's fine.

I see. Ideally I think we shouldn't give the capability of setting the initial UI state in the middleware though.

I renamed the method `EXEPRIMENTAL_use` for now. We can reiterate on this once we roll it out and find more use cases.
